items.title: Microsoft Learn: Activate Azure Credits
items.claim: Microsoft’s activation guide describes the same no-referral route but says it provides USD 1,000 in starter Azure credits, conflicting with the USD 200 figure in its application guide. It says country or region selection controls availability and payment information is required.

items.title: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft for Startups?
items.claim: Microsoft says eligible privately held, for-profit software startups in supported Azure countries may apply directly, and can unlock up to USD 150,000 in Startup credits over time based on verified progress, service adoption, and sustained Azure usage. Investor Network backing may unlock benefits earlier; the ceiling is not an entry entitlement.

items.title: Open Technology Fund: Internet Freedom Fund
items.claim: OTF says its Internet Freedom Fund accepts rolling applications from individuals and organisations for defined internet-freedom projects. It publishes awards between USD 10,000 and USD 900,000 for up to 24 months, paid through performance-based contracts. Its process starts with a Concept Note, and it estimates a response in 6–8 weeks. Applicants in countries subject to applicable United States trade restrictions or export sanctions are excluded.

items.title: Open Technology Fund application portal
items.claim: The live OTF portal says it is continually seeking ideas from individuals and organisations globally defending freedom of expression online and presents an application route for the Internet Freedom Fund.

items.title: Cloudflare for Startups
items.claim: Cloudflare presents USD 10,000 Tier 3 for a bootstrapped or self-funded startup under USD 1 million raised, while its general qualification list also says a startup must have been funded within the last 12 months. It states credits last one year or until consumed, review typically takes up to 48 hours, product caps and exclusions apply, a payment method is required, and overages or post-expiry use can be billed.

items.title: DigitalOcean Startups
items.claim: DigitalOcean says it prioritises AI-native startups, excludes service businesses, and lists USD 10 million or less raised, a company website and associated email, plus a registered DigitalOcean team account using a business email as new-applicant criteria. It says a founder without a VC, incubator, or accelerator can submit by selecting “Other.” The page says credits last 12 months, amount varies, and standard credits exclude listed GPU products and third-party AI models hosted outside DigitalOcean infrastructure.

items.title: DigitalOcean Hatch Terms of Service
items.claim: DigitalOcean says acceptance is discretionary, accepted participants receive a fixed monthly credit amount, unused credits expire one year after acceptance, and overages can be charged.

items.title: UKRI: Transformative sustainable AI technologies
items.claim: UKRI says the opportunity is open until 10 November 2026 at 16:00 UK time. It welcomes research groups and individuals, but requires a project lead based at a UK research organisation eligible for UKRI funding and a role meeting individual eligibility rules. Project full economic cost can be up to GBP 602,500; UKRI will fund 80%.

items.title: MongoDB for Startups
items.claim: MongoDB says its direct base tier looks for startups under seven years old, Series A or earlier, building one scalable software product or service, new to the programme, and publicly established with an active company website and LinkedIn profile. Founders without a VC, accelerator, or incubator may apply directly; accepted startups have 12 months to activate their promo code and 12 months after activation to use Atlas credits. The reviewed page does not publish the base-tier credit amount or geographic coverage.

items.title: Vercel for Startups: credits and FAQ
items.claim: Vercel says approved Startup Partner-affiliated, Series A-or-earlier startups that apply within 12 months of their latest funding can receive a partner-specific Flexible Commitment up to USD 30,000. The commitment lasts up to one year or until used, has a 50% AI Gateway limit, and standard billing follows after it ends.

items.title: NLnet: Apply for funding
items.claim: NLnet says individuals can apply in principle, first grants range from EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000, and open-call deadlines fall on the third day of each odd month; its open-licence condition applies to work developed with the grant.

items.title: NLnet: Apply for a grant
items.claim: NLnet lists its next deadline as 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET and sets the first-grant request range at EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000.

items.title: NLnet Restack Eligibility
items.claim: Restack has no categorical exclusion of persons, gives priority to EU and Horizon Europe-associated applicants, and allows an exceptional applicant outside those areas with a clear European dimension.

items.title: Google for Startups: Pre-funded
items.claim: Google lists USD 2,000 in Cloud credits valid for 12 months for eligible Start-tier startups and states the working-MVP, 24-month founding, prior-credit, billing-account, and matching-domain-email conditions.

items.title: Google for Startups Cloud Program FAQ
items.claim: Google identifies Start as the working-MVP route and Scale as the VC-funded route; programme credits can reach USD 200,000, or USD 350,000 for Scale-tier AI startups.

items.title: AWS Free Tier FAQs
items.claim: New customers can receive up to USD 200 in AWS Free Tier credits; the FAQ states USD 100 at sign-up and up to USD 100 more through qualifying exploration.

items.title: Google Cloud Free Program
items.claim: Eligible new users receive USD 300 in Welcome credit for 90 days, subject to the published prior-customer and verification rules.

items.title: Azure account options
items.claim: Azure lists USD 200 to use on Azure services within 30 days for a new Azure customer free account.

items.title: AWS Activate Credits
items.claim: AWS lists self-funded Founders credits starting at USD 1,000, up to USD 5,000 for selected participants, and a Portfolio tier up to USD 200,000 with an Activate Provider Organization ID.

items.title: Microsoft Learn: Microsoft for Startups application process
items.claim: Microsoft documents a no-referral route that continues to Azure account creation and says its direct starter balance is USD 200. It says a submitted application is reviewed within three business days, requests account and payment details, and says sponsorship moves to pay-as-you-go after credit use or expiry. Its own activation guide shows a conflicting USD 1,000 direct starter balance.

items.title: Azure for Students offer details
items.claim: Microsoft says eligible full-time university students age 18 or older can receive USD 100 in Azure credits within 12 months without a card at sign-up; it publishes the academic-email, one-subscription, use, and exclusion conditions.

items.title: Azure free account comparison
items.claim: Microsoft presents Azure for Startups as USD 1,000 instantly for a new Azure customer and up to USD 5,000 after business verification, with 90-day initial and 180-day post-verification credit windows and pay-as-you-go after expiry or use.

items.title: GitHub Student Developer Pack terms
items.claim: GitHub says third-party Student Developer Pack offers have their own terms, may not stack, and can change or be disrupted.

items.title: AWS Activate Credits
items.claim: AWS lists a self-funded Founders route starting at USD 1,000 and up to USD 5,000 for selected participants, plus a Portfolio route up to USD 200,000 that requires an Activate Provider Organization ID. The page lists pre-Series B status, a Paid Tier Plan, a ten-year founding limit, and new-or-higher-credit conditions.

items.title: Applying for AWS Activate Credits
items.claim: AWS says Founders eligibility includes a fully functioning company website, self-funding, new-to-Activate status, and a founding date within 10 years. It says applicants hear back in 5–10 business days and that Portfolio applicants need a provider Organization ID; where applicable, the most recent funding round must be within 12 months.

items.title: Founder report: Google for Startups application evidence
items.claim: One founder describes public product and team evidence plus several rounds of follow-up during a Google application. This is an individual experience report, not an issuer term, approval guarantee, or typical decision time.

items.title: Oracle Cloud Universal Credits
items.claim: Oracle advertises US$300 in free credits for 30 days and more than 20 Always Free services.

items.title: Sign Up for the Free Oracle Cloud Promotion
items.claim: Oracle documents country, contact and payment verification, one account per email, and an irreversible Home Region choice.

items.title: What Happens When the Promotion Expires
items.claim: Oracle documents a 30-day-or-consumption end point for the promotion and the treatment of paid and Always Free resources afterward.
